title: Launch of new space telescope stirs global science
seoTitle: Launch of new space telescope stirs global science
subtitle: The observatory will be placed into orbit aboard a Falcon Heavy rocket
excerpt: NASA is preparing to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope this Sunday on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket in Florida.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Preparations for the launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope are energizing the space sector and capturing public interest at this moment. The observatory is scheduled to launch on Sunday at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, and will be placed into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket.

Launch and rocket details

The launch is taking place nine months ahead of schedule, according to officials from the US space agency. The equipment costs approximately four billion dollars, and its liftoff will occur at the Kennedy Space Center, powered by a Falcon Heavy rocket.

Space mission objectives

The tool was designed to explore vast regions of the sky and deepen studies on dark matter, dark energy, and Earth-like exoplanets. Scientists intend to use the mission to test gravity on vast scales and search for planets beyond the solar system, covering more than two billion galaxies during their research.

Military origin of the hardware

The structure of the Roman was not initially created for space exploration. Following the attacks on New York's Twin Towers in 2001, the US National Reconnaissance Office requested the creation of extremely powerful telescopes for Earth observation. Years later, part of the program was canceled, and the machines were stored and offered to NASA in 2012.

Comparison with other telescopes

Roman is the successor to the Hubble Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope. It will form a new triad of observatories capable of observing different details of the universe, offering a panoramic view and high scanning speed that allow studying the cosmos through wide-field surveys.

With information from VEJA, Forbes Brasil.
